gaps.term: r exceeds every fixed power of p
gaps.quote: Both are $o(Tp)$ because $r$ exceeds every fixed power of $p$.
gaps.note: The page only gives an upper bound r <= 2^{O(p/d)}. That r grows faster than every power of p needs a lower bound such as log r = Theta(p^{1-epsilon}), which the page does not state or derive. It only has l = Theta(p^{1-epsilon}) and r = 2^l if the reader links them.

The step from p^{1-kappa} to (log n)^{1-kappa}, and the claims p^{A+C}=o(Tp) and the polylog bounds, need p = Theta(log n) (p = 6 ceil(log2 n) in the paper). The page never states how p relates to n, only V=Tp=Theta(n).

gaps.term: stable bit sorting of exceptional records
gaps.quote: Stable bit sorting makes $O(p)$ scans of it
gaps.note: The page does not say what the O(p)-bit key is used for, what is sorted by it, or why sorting by one bit per scan on a tape machine gives O(p) linear scans. The reader cannot check this cost.
